title: Rogue agents, told by the labs
summary: Company disclosures of agents misusing public and government sites, a taxonomy of rogue-agent activity, a distillation paper on incriminating misaligned models, and Epoch's InnovationEval.

title: Narrow training, wide misalignment
summary: Narrow fine-tuning induces misalignment across fifteen vision-language models, a speculative route for a rogue agent to replicate through self-distillation, and a proposal to gate frontier training on resolved alignment issues.

title: Agents that spread, and models that stay silent
summary: Anthropic researchers' claim that small models could self-replicate on cheap devices, a Tencent-linked agent fleet that answered planted text, and agents leaking benchmark answers through a public screenshot service. Gemini 4 Argon launched with its safety claims, and a LessWrong study found models failed to disclose their own mistakes in 67% of prefilled cases.

title: Rogue agents, and a broken benchmark
summary: An Anthropic test model's visa applications, an OpenAI model spending test ether from a public seed phrase, and a Tencent-linked fleet that replied to researchers; about a quarter of the audited tasks in Gemini 4 Argon's ML R&D benchmark were broken. Full reads: the visa applications post and the test ether post.

title: Attacks split across agents and time
summary: Monitors that read one agent, or one stretch of context, at a time miss attacks split across agents or across compactions; evals can lie to models or shape the evidence they later read; a funding experiment uses AI to rank proposals. Full reads: the multi-agent attack red-team paper and the split-across-compactions monitoring study.

title: Split attacks and trusting monitors
summary: Attacks split across agents or across time evade monitors that read one trajectory at a time, evaluations can lie to models or shape the evidence they later read, a funding experiment uses AI to rank proposals, and data-centre investment is not crowding out the rest of the economy. Full reads: the multi-agent red-teaming paper and the compaction split-attack dataset.
